$comment: Orcivo orchestration SECURITY SPINE (V2) config. V2 is a clean-room rebuild after the independent review REJECTED V1, then a second review REJECTED the V1 spine. This file holds knobs, NEVER status. V2 runtime state lives under .orchestration/v2/ and is authoritative for V2 only. V1 runtime state is never read by V2. Nothing here is controllable by a task spec.

ledger.$comment: C-01: WAITING_HUMAN is NOT dispatchable - a task parked for a human is resumed only by an explicit gate approval event, never by the scheduler. Any ledger corruption -> QUARANTINED (fail closed), never a 'plausible' rebuild.

contract.$comment: H-06/M-01: an empty declaredScope FAILS CLOSED (no changed file is in scope). An unrestricted executor needs the explicit risk-C grant 'unrestrictedScope', which is a different thing from []. H3-05: a protectedPathGrant MUST be an exact canonical member of grantableProtectedPrefixes - no globs, no root, no parent, no 'whole .planning'. A task can never invent a new protected prefix. prisma/schema.prisma is grantable only as that exact file on an elevated-risk contract; prisma/ and sibling paths remain ungrantable.

preflight.$comment: M3-03: the fetch observation is in-process authority only. Invoke-PreflightFetch mints a session token; Test-Preflight requires the exact in-memory object, performed=true, exit 0, correct remote/target/beforeSHA, a non-empty freshly-observed remote SHA, and NO 'NO_REMOTE' dispatch path. A writable last-fetch.json is audit-only and never authority. #9: the derived index entry must agree with the frozen contract on taskId, gate and dependencies - a derived index can never weaken a frozen contract.

limits.$comment: C-02/H-03: hard bounds enforced BEFORE and DURING schema validation. Anything over the bound fails closed to HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED.

verification.$comment: NH-02: verification is DECLARATIVE and lives here, outside any task. A task names a profileId; it cannot supply commands, executables, args, cwd or env. The frozen contract binds verificationDefinitionHash = canonical hash of the resolved profile object below.

A.description: docs / copy / fixture - structural checks only, no build

B.description: contained code change - structural + lint-shape checks (no network)

C.description: security / tenant / money / schema - full checks, human gate required elsewhere

classification.$comment: H-01: provider failover is allowed ONLY for these classes, and ONLY when the class comes from the CLI's own structured control channel - never from application/task/test stdout.

leases.$comment: H-05: a lease whose holder process is provably alive is NEVER an orphan, regardless of heartbeat age. A stale heartbeat alone quarantines the lease record; it does not hand the key to a second writer.

gates.$comment: #13: on read, gateHash is recomputed over {gateId, taskVersionId, specHash, decision, approvalIdentity, approvalTimestamp, nonce}. Synthetic approvals are permitted ONLY from the isolated test harness (Assert-DisposableRoot).

threatModel.$comment: PRAGMATIC V2.1 - OWNER DECISION (2026-09-03). The owner's local Windows host and Windows user account are TRUSTED. The harness defends against what the LLM agents and candidate-controlled code do wrong, NOT against an attacker who already holds the owner's access. This is a knob only in the sense that code reads `id` and `outOfScope`; the authoritative narrative lives in docs/agents/ORCHESTRATION-THREAT-MODEL.md and .planning/reviews/PRAGMATIC-V2.1-CLOSEOUT.md.

zoneSeparation.containment: disposable Docker Linux for implementer/test/reviewer when execution is technically possible; the worktree/clone is a scope boundary, not a claimed host security boundary

acceptedRisks.title: verified process-tree kill on timeout
acceptedRisks.reason: same-user trusted host; a surviving child of a timed-out agent is a reliability nuisance, not privilege escalation. Kept: direct-child kill + lease quarantine + run marked non-integratable.

acceptedRisks.title: OS-enforced host isolation of executor/reviewer/integrator by SID/service
acceptedRisks.reason: LOCAL_TRUSTED_HOST: executor already runs as the trusted owner. Docker Linux is the containment mechanism when execution is possible; the worktree is a scope boundary only.

acceptedRisks.title: coherently self-hashed rewrite of a frozen contract file / closed-world schema
acceptedRisks.reason: requires writing .orchestration/v2/contracts/*.json on the trusted host = HOST_SAME_USER_ATTACKER. Contract immutability still blocks the LLM, which cannot reach the authority namespace.

acceptedRisks.title: in-process authority-token / lease-quarantine-recovery forgery from a hostile same-user process
acceptedRisks.reason: mutating the supervisor's in-memory PowerShell scope or replaying a recovery token requires code execution as the owner. Cheap hardening (atomic recovery, token hashing) kept.

acceptedRisks.title: Zone A/D single Windows SID; NTFS junction redirection of the authority's own out-of-band files
acceptedRisks.reason: OWNER: ZONE_A_D_SEPARATE_WINDOWS_IDENTITIES = NOT_REQUIRED. Redirecting the authority's own files is host tampering.

acceptedRisks.title: host Docker daemon launch authority not modeled

taskClassifier.$comment: PARTE 11. Difficulty is SEMANTIC, not counted from LOC / path / extension / function count. A classifier agent with structured output is preferred; the deterministic scorer is the fallback and the Wave 0 authority. The rules below are ONLY safety floors / caps.

router.$comment: PARTE 12. Abstract profiles resolve at RUNTIME against the actually-installed CLIs. NO permanent hardcoded model version. Discovered capabilities cache in state/cli-capabilities.json, refreshed when the CLI --version string changes. If a CLI cannot select reasoning/effort explicitly, use the best supported mechanism and record the limitation.

knownCapabilities.$comment: PARTE 12 fallback ONLY. Used to fill a gap the live --help probe could not read (e.g. codex exec --help needing a TTY). The probe result always wins when it is non-null; anything filled from here is listed in the route limitations.

providerFailover.$comment: PARTE 13/14/15. Automatic provider switch ONLY for a class in classification.providerClasses coming from the control channel. TEST_FAILED / BUG / BUILD_FAILED / REVIEW_REQUEST_CHANGES / INVALID_IMPLEMENTATION never fail over. All enabled providers unavailable -> WAITING_PROVIDER; the supervisor keeps polling and auto-resumes with no human action.

contextExhaustion.$comment: PARTE 15. Context exhaustion is NOT quota and NEVER fails over. A context limit -> structured continuation checkpoint + fresh invocation, same task lineage, no hidden chain-of-thought carried.

correctionLoop.$comment: PARTE 17. REQUEST_CHANGES -> structured findings -> implementer -> NEW candidate -> rerun checks -> new review. Bounded; no infinite loop.

integrationIntent.$comment: PARTE 8. A durable INTEGRATION_INTENT is written BEFORE any git publication. origin is the FINAL truth of publication. After timeout / connection drop / push failure / crash / uncertain exit / post-push ledger failure -> FETCH REMOTE, compare SHA/tree, reconstruct truth, THEN set a terminal state. Never report NOT_PUBLISHED while remote truth is unknown. Never auto-republish something already confirmed in origin.

generation.$comment: PARTE 9. Each execution gets a fencing generation. Before RECOVERED: detect stale/failed owner -> stop / verify inactive -> fence old generation -> RECOVERED -> new generation. Never RECOVERED then check. If undeterminable -> QUARANTINED or WAITING_HUMAN.

pilot.$comment: PILOT MODE (2026-09-03). The guarded supervisor loop. runnerMode defaults to inproc-fake: the pilot validates the full autonomous lifecycle + every guard against SYNTHETIC disposable tasks with no model calls. 'docker' runs real agents / candidate code in a disposable Linux container (infra/orchestration/). 'host-trusted' runs real agents on the trusted host (LOCAL_TRUSTED_HOST / AR-02) - candidate-controlled build/test still never runs in the supervisor process. A real PB1-* task additionally requires realExecutionAuthFile to exist AND its P02/P03 gates satisfied AND (for Level C) an owner gate; the pilot never lifts those on its own.

memoryAdapter.$comment: ai-memory 2.x adapter seam. Memory is AUXILIARY: never authority (task manifest > acceptance > planning > candidate/Git > verification/review > memory), fail-soft (any adapter error is ignored and dispatch continues), implementer-prompt-only (reviewers never receive it). Owner approved enabling this on 2026-09-04 (see .planning/reviews/AI-MEMORY-2-MIGRATION.md). Reference adapter: scripts/orchestration/v2/memory-eval-adapter.ps1. Logical project identity is ALWAYS `project` here / ORCIVO_MEMORY_PROJECT, never a working-directory basename. Bounded retrieval: <= maxMemories pages and <= maxInjectChars chars, only paths under injectKinds, latest-version-only (ai-memory native), injected as untrusted background.

redaction.$comment: H3-02: ONE canonical secret library. `secretPatterns` is used identically by the streaming redactor (Protect-Line), the sanitize-before-write path, the pre-publication scan gate AND the final artifact sweep. `multilinePatterns` is the stateful PEM buffer. Every value-capturing pattern includes its key/prefix in the match so a `[REDACTED]` replacement removes the trigger and a redacted artifact scans clean.
redaction.$comment2: H4-03 (in-scope under LOCAL_TRUSTED_HOST: secret-published-by-accident). The pre-publication scan decodes UTF-8 / UTF-16LE / UTF-16BE (BOM and no-BOM) and also scans the exact COMMITTED candidate blob bytes via git, not only worktree files. Unknown / unreadable dangerous input fails closed.
